strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear practical relevance: Identifies two concrete challenges in augmented LLM serving (HoL blocking and fixed batch budgets) with compelling empirical evidence (Figures 2-4). Augmented LLMs are increasingly prevalent, making this timely and important.

Technically sound and well-designed approach: The request lifecycle model appropriately captures multi-stage execution with external calls. The space-time cost model provides a unified metric for heterogeneous phases. Pre-invocation estimation + post-invocation refinement elegantly mitigates prediction errors using runtime feedback.

Exceptionally comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple models (6B-70B), GPUs, and datasets. Diverse workloads and extensive metrics. Thorough ablation study showing both components are necessary. Robustness analysis to prediction errors (10-50%), bursty arrivals. Extended appendices with additional baselines (MARS) and implementations.

Substantial and convincing performance gains: 6.5× geometric mean goodput improvement, 95.6% TTFT reduction. Particularly pronounced under high load where HoL blocking is severe. Clear demonstration via latency breakdown (Figure 9) that gains come from queuing time reduction.

Clear presentation and documentation: Well-motivated early figures. Clear system architecture and algorithm pseudocode. Comprehensive notation table and formal problem formulation. Extensive appendices with additional results.

Practical implementation: Built on vLLM for real-world applicability. Scheduling overhead remains small (<0.03s even with 200+ paused requests). Details on prediction, cost estimation, and budget adaptation provided.
weaknesses: Prediction accuracy concerns: Output length achieves only 65% bucket accuracy on INFERCEPT (lower than 85% on ToolBench). External call duration MSE of 5s on ToolBench could be significant. While robustness to ±10-50% synthetic errors is shown (§6.3), actual error distributions may differ. Limited discussion of how prediction inaccuracy affects scheduling quality.

Limited algorithmic novelty: Space-time cost model is straightforward formalization. Value-density greedy knapsack is standard. Context-handling policy selection (Eqs. 12-15) is adapted from INFERCEPT. Main novelty is integration with state-aware refinement, which is incremental. Core differences vs. MARS (D.6) are modest.

Weak theoretical guarantees: Theorem E.1 provides only 1/2-approximation for simplified per-iteration problem with fixed values/costs. Does not extend to full online, multi-stage problem where costs evolve and decisions are continuously refined. No formal guarantees for complete algorithm. Gap between theory and practice.

Evaluation fairness concerns: SLO thresholds (TTFT<1s) not discussed as potentially favoring AugServe. Baselines (vLLM, INFERCEPT) not designed for SLO-aware augmented LLM serving; at high load, goodput drops due to SLO violations rather than capacity limits. SSJF baseline uses AugServe's predictor (advantage to AugServe). No error bars or statistical significance testing reported.

Non-negligible and growing scheduling overhead: AugServe adds ~40% more overhead than INFERCEPT (0.018s vs 0.013s at 3.0 req/s). Overhead scales with paused requests (Table 6: up to 0.025s with 150-200 paused requests). Could become bottleneck at extreme loads. Trade-off deserves more discussion.

Limited discussion of limitations and failure modes: No analysis of scenarios where approach underperforms. How does it handle external call failures, timeouts, or highly unpredictable durations? What if predictions are systematically biased? No worst-case analysis.

Incomplete reproducibility details: How is instantaneous memory occupancy m_i(t, p_i) computed in practice? Prediction model fine-tuning details sparse (hyperparameters, data splits, convergence). No mention of code availability. Implementation details for space-time cost computation incomplete.

Hyperparameter tuning guidance incomplete: β sensitivity analyzed (Table D.3) showing acceptable range [10^-5, 10^-4], but βlow, βhigh, and Tmax have minimal discussion. How were these chosen? Are they workload-dependent? Limited guidance for new deployments.

Specialized problem domain: Approach tailored to augmented LLM serving; generalization to other workloads with external calls unclear. Contribution is practically important but specialized compared to general LLM inference optimization.

Unstated memory model assumptions: Space-time cost assumes deterministic per-token footprint μ and linear memory growth. In practice, KV cache may have overheads (padding, fragmentation) not scaling linearly. Impact on scheduling quality not analyzed.
